summary: Hajime Kitamura (1923–2003) was a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at Shizuoka High School and the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada, later holding posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986) and Reitaku University (~1986–1991).

Hajime Nakamura (1912–1999) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui. He served as associate professor there (1943–1973) and directed the Eastern Institute and Tōhō Gakuin (~1973–1999).

Hajime Okayama (1948–2022) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Peking University, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences under Xianlin Ji, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (1995–2012).

Hajime Sakurabe (1925–2012) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, later serving as professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1960) and Otani University (1971–1986).

Hajime Tanabe (1885–1962) was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, Kyoto University under Kitarō Nishida, and in Germany under Edmund Husserl, Heinrich Rickert, and Martin Heidegger, later teaching at Kyoto University (1919–1945).
Hakuin Ekaku (1686–1769) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Dōkyō Etan and Hakuyūshi, and taught Suiō Genro.

Hakuju Ui (1882–1963) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and in Europe under Richard von Garbe, later teaching at Tohoku University and the University of Tokyo (1930–1943).

Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani (1885–1973) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy figure. He studied at Toshima Normal School and trained under teachers including Sogaku Daiun Harada, Bokusan Nishiari, Kodo Akino, Ian Kishizawa, and Tatsugen Nozawa, later founding Sanbo Zen in 1954.
Halle O'Neal specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas under the supervision of Sherry Fowler.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa (1914–1990) specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, SOAS, the University of Toronto, and served as head of the London Buddhist Vihara (1957–1990).
Hank Glassman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, holding posts on the faculty at Haverford College, as attested in 2009 and 2019.

Hanns Oertel (1868–1952) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Yale (1891–1917), the University of Marburg (1922), and the University of Munich (1925–1935).

Hanns-Peter Schmidt (1930–2017) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and served as professor at the University of California, Los Angeles (1965–2000).
Hans Delbrück (1848–1929) was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869–1873) and held a post at the University of Berlin beginning in 1885.

Hans Harder (born 1966) is an Indologist who studied at the universities of Hamburg and Heidelberg, completing his doctorate under Rahul Peter Das and his habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, where he was an assistant (1995–2007).

Hans Hartog (born 1912) is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Marburg under Friedrich Heiler after studies at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Bethel, and Munich under Hanns Oertel, Walther Wüst, Ferdinand Sommer, and others.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder (1896–1957) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (~1930–1931), University of Berlin (~1931–1945), and University of Göttingen (~1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock (born 1938) is a linguist and Indologist. He completed graduate degrees at Northwestern University and Yale University, where he studied under Warren Cowgill, and served as professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1967–2013).
Hans Krahe (1898–1965) was a linguist who held posts at the University of Würzburg (~1936–1946), the University of Heidelberg (~1947–1949), and the University of Tübingen (~1949–1965).

Hans Küng (1928–2021) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum, and the Catholic University of Paris, and held a post at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1996).
